title: Back-to-Back Habibi: Kaushal Repeats in Buckaroo Bowl II While Sonny Holds the Basement Keys Again
dek: The Habibsters went 11-3, flattened Brucie by 116 points in Buckaroo Bowl II, and turned a two-year-old league into a dynasty, while Ben Dover finished last for the second straight season.
body: Year two of the Buckaroo Football League opened with a statement from the least likely corner of the room. Ramon's Araleasers dropped 166.58 points in Week 1, the highest single week of the entire 2024 season, and for one glorious Sunday Brucie looked like the guy who had cracked the code. It was the kind of opening act that makes you rethink everything you believed in August. Spoiler: the rest of the league eventually remembered who won the first trophy.

That would be Kaushal, who spent the regular season making defense of a title look like a Saturday in Athens with a top-five ranking. The Habibsters went 11-3, scored 1,524.8 points, and locked up the No. 1 seed again. No other team won more than eight games. Habibi didn't just have a good roster; he had the rare fantasy gift of scoring big in the weeks it mattered and letting everyone else waste their best games on each other.

The most baffling stat line of 2024 belongs to Randy. The fumblers led the league with 1,595.1 points, 70 more than the champion, and went a respectable 8-6 to grab the second seed. Then the playoffs arrived and Ramon's Araleasers bounced them 202.44 to 176.14 over two weeks. Randy now owns the league's points crown and absolutely nothing to show for it, which, for a Chicago football fan, is at least a familiar feeling. Expect the complaints to arrive in the group chat roughly every hour until the 2025 draft.

Alan snuck into the playoffs as the No. 4 seed at 6-8, a losing record carried in on the back of 1,473.9 points, third-most in the league. Philliberto's reward was a date with the Habibsters, and Kaushal won it 296.96 to 245.08. Philly did salvage third place, which means the league's resident jerk finished ahead of the team that scored the most points. Somewhere, Randy is still filing a grievance about that, and somewhere, Alan is enjoying it.

Buckaroo Bowl II was billed as Brucie's chance to finish what Week 1 started. Instead, it was a two-week demolition: Habibsters 261.44, Araleasers 145.28. That 116-point margin is less a championship game and more a public service announcement about volatility. Credit Ramon for a 7-7 season that turned into a title-game appearance, but anyone who has watched him lose a video game knows those two weeks probably did not go quietly in the Araleasers household.

At the bottom, Mekhi's Dawgs and Sonny's Ben Dover both finished 5-9, but the numbers told different stories. Kai put up 1,413.5 points, respectable enough to have stolen a few more wins with better luck, and he climbed out of the cellar to finish fifth. Sonny was not so fortunate. Ben Dover scored a league-low 1,304.3 points and posted the season's worst week, a brutal 44.1 in Week 12, which is a number you usually see on a thermostat in a New England winter, not a fantasy scoreboard. The commissioner finished last for the second straight year, and nobody can accuse him of rigging the league in his own favor.

Like 2023, the season closed with zero trades, so every result came straight from draft day and the waiver wire. That leaves the Buckaroo Football League two years old with one name on the trophy, twice. Kaushal is the standard, Randy has the points and the grudge, Alan has a bronze he will mention constantly, and Sonny has a basement he knows a little too well. Somebody is going to have to knock Habibi off the throne, and as of now, nobody has figured out how.
